questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

In an arithmetic progression (AP), each term is obtained by adding a fixed number (the common difference d) to the previous term. The first term is a.

(i) Identify the AP 3, 7, 11, 15, ... — find a and d.
(ii) State the formula for the n-th term.
(iii) Find the 20th term.
(iv) Which term of the AP is 99?
questions.answer:
(i) First term a = 3; common difference d = 7 − 3 = 4.
(ii) aₙ = a + (n − 1)d.
(iii) a₂₀ = 3 + 19·4 = 3 + 76 = 79.
(iv) 99 = 3 + (n − 1)·4 ⇒ 96 = 4(n − 1) ⇒ n − 1 = 24 ⇒ n = 25. So 99 is the 25th term.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

The 4th term of an AP is 14 and the 10th term is 32.

(i) Use the n-th term formula to set up two equations.
(ii) Solve for a and d.
(iii) Find the first three terms.
(iv) Find the 25th term.
questions.answer:
(i) a₄ = a + 3d = 14 and a₁₀ = a + 9d = 32.
(ii) Subtract: 6d = 18 ⇒ d = 3. Then a = 14 − 9 = 5.
(iii) First three terms: 5, 8, 11.
(iv) a₂₅ = 5 + 24·3 = 5 + 72 = 77.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Find the sum of first 20 terms of the AP 2, 6, 10, 14, ...

(i) Identify a and d.
(ii) State the formula for the sum of the first n terms.
(iii) Compute the sum.
(iv) Find the sum of all natural numbers from 1 to 100.

Read the passage and answer the questions.

A student saves ₹100 in the first month and increases the saving by ₹50 each subsequent month.

(i) Write the savings in months 1, 2, 3.
(ii) Identify the AP and its a, d.
(iii) Total saving in 12 months?
(iv) When does the monthly saving first exceed ₹500?

Read the passage and answer the questions.

The sum of the first 7 terms of an AP is 49, and the sum of the first 17 terms is 289.

(i) Use the sum formula to set up two equations.
(ii) Solve for a and d.
(iii) Find the AP's first three terms.
(iv) Find the sum of the first 25 terms.
questions.answer:
(i) S₇ = 7/2 · [2a + 6d] = 7(a + 3d) = 49 ⇒ a + 3d = 7. S₁₇ = 17/2 · [2a + 16d] = 17(a + 8d) = 289 ⇒ a + 8d = 17.
(ii) Subtract: 5d = 10 ⇒ d = 2. Then a = 7 − 6 = 1.
(iii) First three terms: 1, 3, 5 (the odd natural numbers).
(iv) S₂₅ = 25/2 · [2·1 + 24·2] = 25/2 · 50 = 625. (This is also 25² — sum of first 25 odd numbers = 25².)

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Which of the following sequences is an AP?
• A: 2, 4, 8, 16, ...
• B: 1, 4, 9, 16, ...
• C: 5, 8, 11, 14, ...
• D: 100, 90, 80, 70, ...

(i) For each, compute consecutive differences.
(ii) Which sequences are APs?
(iii) For the APs, state d.
(iv) For A, what kind of progression is it?
questions.answer:
(i) A: 4−2=2, 8−4=4, 16−8=8 (not constant). B: 4−1=3, 9−4=5, 16−9=7 (not constant). C: 8−5=3, 11−8=3, 14−11=3 (constant). D: 90−100=−10, 80−90=−10, 70−80=−10 (constant).
(ii) APs: C and D.
(iii) For C: d = 3. For D: d = −10 (decreasing AP).
(iv) Sequence A doubles each time — it's a GEOMETRIC progression with common ratio 2 (not an AP).

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

In an AP, the 5th term is twice the 2nd term and the 8th term is 30.

(i) Express the conditions as equations in a and d.
(ii) Solve them.
(iii) Write the first five terms.
(iv) Find the sum of the first 20 terms.

Read the passage and answer the questions.

A stack of logs is arranged with 20 logs in the bottom row, 19 in the next, 18 in the next, and so on.

(i) Write the AP for the number of logs row by row.
(ii) How many rows are needed if there are 200 logs in total?
(iii) How many logs are in the top row?
(iv) Is the stack triangular in shape? Explain.
questions.answer:
(i) AP: 20, 19, 18, ..., with a = 20, d = −1.
(ii) Sₙ = n/2 · [2a + (n − 1)d] = n/2 · [40 − (n − 1)] = n/2 · (41 − n) = 200 ⇒ n(41 − n) = 400 ⇒ n² − 41n + 400 = 0. D = 1681 − 1600 = 81. n = (41 ± 9)/2 ⇒ n = 25 or n = 16. n = 25 gives negative logs in top row (impossible), so n = 16.
(iii) Top row: a₁₆ = 20 + 15(−1) = 5 logs.
(iv) Yes — each row up has fewer logs than the previous, forming a triangular cross-section.
